info.desc: Blood Sugar Sex Magik is the fifth studio album by American alternative rock band Red Hot Chili Peppers, released on September 24, 1991. Produced by Rick Rubin, it was the band's first record released on Warner Bros. Records. The musical styles of Blood Sugar Sex Magik differed notably from the techniques employed on the band's preceding album, Mother's Milk (1989), and featured little use of heavy metal guitar riffs. The album's subject matter incorporated sexual innuendos and references to drugs and death as well as themes of lust and exuberance. The album has sold over seven million copies in the .

podcast.body: Released on September 24, 1991, the same day as Nirvana's "Nevermind," this album established the Red Hot Chili Peppers as global superstars. Recorded with new guitarist John Frusciante and producer Rick Rubin under a new deal with Warner Brothers, it sold at least 14 million copies in the US, 1.5 million in the UK, and nearly 500,000 in Canada, also being a major seller in Germany, Australia, and New Zealand. The album was rich with singles and was marketed under the alternative label, despite its sound not being grunge. "this record that set them up as global superstars for the next quarter century."

podcast.body: Released on September 24, 1991, this album was the first to feature John Frusciante as guitarist. It propelled the band from a "mid-level" group to one of the biggest acts of the alternative era, selling over 15 million copies and spawning six singles. The band switched from EMI to Warner Records and replaced producer Michael Beinhorn with Rick Rubin for this record. It was recorded in a historic, isolated, and reportedly haunted mansion in Laurel Canyon, which Rick Rubin converted into a studio, with John Frusciante embracing its eerie atmosphere. "That record is sold somewhere beyond 15 million copies, and that would have never, ever happened without John."

podcast.body: The band recorded this album in a house rumored to be haunted, leading to guitarist John Frusciante incorporating "ghostly bits" into the music using a 1958 Stratocaster. This anecdote explains the spooky, stunning musical elements attributed to John Frusciante's playing on the album. "Laura has it that the house where the chili peppers recorded blood sugar-sex magic was haunted, hence the spooky stunning bits from John."
